questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (stage of meiosis) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Metaphase I
B. Telophase I
C. Prophase II
D. Anaphase II

List-II:
I. The centromere of each chromosome splits and the sister chromatids move towards opposite poles
II. The nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear; cytokinesis follows to form a dyad of cells
III. The bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate
IV. The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of this stage and the chromosomes again become compact

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Stages of meiosis I and II
solution.explanation: In metaphase I the bivalents align on the equatorial plate. In telophase I the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear and cytokinesis gives a dyad of cells. In prophase II the nuclear membrane disappears by the end and chromosomes compact again. Anaphase II begins with simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome, so sister chromatids move to opposite poles.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap telophase I with prophase II, metaphase I with anaphase II, or metaphase I with telophase I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I; Meiosis II)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mitosis is also called equational division.
Reason (R): In mitosis, the number of chromosomes in the parent cell and in the progeny cells is the same.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Since the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, mitosis is called equational division. R is the very reason for the name.
steps: R: true and is the reason for the name → A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the cell cycle are correct?

(a) Interphase lasts more than 95 per cent of the duration of the cell cycle.
(b) Some cells in adult animals, such as heart cells, do not appear to divide.
(c) Interphase is divided into the G1, S and M phases.
(d) The G1 phase is the interval between mitosis and the initiation of DNA replication.
(e) The G2 phase is the interval between the S phase and the G1 phase.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Interphase lasts more than 95% of the cycle and is divided into G1, S and G2. G1 lies between mitosis and the start of DNA replication; G2 lies between S and the M phase. Some adult animal cells, e.g., heart cells, do not appear to divide.
steps: (e) false: G2 lies between S and M
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of cell cycle)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: At metaphase of mitosis, the two sister chromatids of a chromosome are attached by their kinetochores to spindle fibres:

options.text: at their arms rather than at the kinetochores
only one chromatid is attached; the other is free

solution.explanation: At metaphase, all chromosomes lie at the equator. One chromatid of each chromosome is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole, and its sister chromatid by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.
steps: Kinetochore of one chromatid → one pole; kinetochore of the sister → opposite pole
solution.why_others_wrong: Attachment to the same pole could not separate the chromatids; spindle fibres attach at kinetochores; both chromatids are attached.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Metaphase)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cell repair by mitosis is seen only in plants; in animals, cells such as those of the upper layer of the epidermis and the lining of the gut are never replaced.
Reason (R): Mitotic divisions in the meristematic tissues, the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a continuous growth of plants throughout their life.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Mitosis also repairs and replaces cells in animals: cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut and blood cells are constantly replaced. So A is false. R is true: mitosis in the apical and lateral cambium gives continuous growth of plants.
steps: A: false, such animal cells are constantly replaced
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Significance of Mitosis
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant has 2n = 18. How many chromosomes and how many chromatids are present in each cell at metaphase II of meiosis?

solution.concept: Chromosome and chromatid number in meiosis II
solution.explanation: Anaphase I separates homologous chromosomes, so each cell after meiosis I has n = 9 chromosomes. The sister chromatids stay joined at the centromere until anaphase II, so at metaphase II each of the 9 chromosomes still has two chromatids.
steps: Each chromosome = 2 sister chromatids until anaphase II
solution.why_others_wrong: 18 and 36 is the count at metaphase of mitosis. 9 and 9 assumes the chromatids have already separated. 18 and 18 forgets the reduction in meiosis I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis II)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about meiosis are correct?

(a) Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division but only a single cycle of DNA replication.
(b) Meiosis I is initiated before the parental chromosomes replicate.
(c) Meiosis involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
(d) Four haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis II.
(e) The prophase of mitosis is typically longer and more complex than prophase I of meiosis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Meiosis has two cycles of division with one round of DNA replication. Meiosis I starts after the chromosomes have replicated in the S phase. Homologues pair and recombine, and meiosis II ends with four haploid cells. Prophase I is typically longer and more complex than the prophase of mitosis.
steps: (b) false: meiosis I starts after replication
(e) false: prophase I is the longer and more complex one
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Each of the two cells formed at the end of meiosis I has half the number of chromosomes of the parent meiocyte.
Reason (R): In anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes separate, while the sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In anaphase I, whole homologous chromosomes (each with two chromatids) move to opposite poles. Each pole therefore receives one member of each pair, so the chromosome number is halved. R is the explanation of A.
steps: Separation of homologues halves the chromosome number → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I: anaphase I)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Yeast can progress through the cell cycle in only about 90 minutes.
Statement II: Although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage of the cell cycle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Duration of the cell cycle; growth versus DNA synthesis
solution.explanation: The duration of the cell cycle varies between organisms and cell types: yeast completes it in about 90 minutes. Cytoplasmic growth is continuous, but DNA is synthesised only in the S phase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Within the chloroplast, the enzymatic reactions that synthesise sugar take place in the:

solution.concept: Division of labour in the chloroplast
solution.explanation: The membrane system (grana and stroma lamellae) traps light energy and makes ATP and NADPH. In the stroma, enzymatic reactions incorporate CO₂ into the plant, leading to the synthesis of sugar, which in turn forms starch.
steps: Light trapping, ATP, NADPH → membrane system
solution.why_others_wrong: The grana carry out the light reactions; the lumen is where protons accumulate; the outer membrane has no role in sugar synthesis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis take place?

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Besides enabling a wider range of wavelengths of incoming light to be used for photosynthesis, the accessory pigments also:

options.text: act as the reaction centre of both photosystems

solution.explanation: Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are accessory pigments. They absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a, and they also protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.
steps: Accessory pigments: widen the usable spectrum + protect chlorophyll a
solution.why_others_wrong: The reaction centre is a chlorophyll a molecule; water splitting is linked to PS II; CO₂ is fixed by RuBisCO, an enzyme.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', How many types of pigments are involved in photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option D: protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The reaction centre of Photosystem II has an absorption peak at:

solution.explanation: In PS I the reaction-centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm (P700); in PS II it has an absorption peak at 680 nm (P680).
solution.why_others_wrong: 700 nm is the peak of PS I. 660 nm and 720 nm are not reaction-centre peaks given by NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is Light Reaction?

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which enzyme is described by NCERT as the most abundant enzyme in the world?

solution.explanation: RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO), which catalyses the carboxylation of RuBP, is the most abundant enzyme in the world.
steps: Most abundant enzyme in the world → RuBisCO
solution.why_others_wrong: PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ in the mesophyll of C4 plants, ATP synthase makes ATP and NADP reductase reduces NADP⁺; none of these is described as the most abundant enzyme.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Photorespiration

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The Calvin cycle occurs only in plants that have the C3 pathway.
Statement II: The Calvin cycle can be described under three stages: carboxylation, reduction and regeneration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The Calvin pathway occurs in all photosynthetic plants, whether they have C3 or C4 pathways. It has three stages: carboxylation of RuBP, reduction to carbohydrate, and regeneration of RuBP.
steps: Statement I: false, it occurs in all photosynthetic plants
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the carboxylation step of the Calvin cycle, how many molecules of RuBP are used and how many molecules of 3-PGA are formed when six molecules of CO₂ are fixed?

solution.explanation: Carboxylation is the fixation of CO₂ into RuBP, catalysed by RuBisCO; each carboxylation gives two molecules of 3-PGA. So each CO₂ uses one RuBP and forms two PGA.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 PGA forgets that each carboxylation yields two PGA. 12 RuBP doubles the RuBP instead of the PGA. 3 RuBP and 6 PGA halves both, as if two CO₂ were fixed per RuBP.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle (Carboxylation)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about C4 plants are correct?

(a) 'Kranz' means 'wreath' and reflects the arrangement of cells around the vascular bundles.
(b) C4 plants tolerate higher temperatures.
(c) Maize and sorghum are examples of C3 plants.
(d) The C4 acid formed in the mesophyll is converted to malic acid or aspartic acid, which is transported to the bundle sheath cells.
(e) C4 plants show a poor response to high light intensities.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: C4 plants such as maize and sorghum have Kranz anatomy ('wreath' of bundle sheath cells). They tolerate higher temperatures and respond to high light intensities. OAA formed in the mesophyll is converted to malic or aspartic acid, which moves to the bundle sheath.
steps: (e) false: they respond to high light intensities
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When CO₂ and O₂ are present in nearly equal concentrations, RuBisCO has a greater affinity for O₂ than for CO₂.
Reason (R): The active site of RuBisCO can bind both CO₂ and O₂, and the relative concentration of O₂ and CO₂ determines which of the two will bind to the enzyme.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: RuBisCO's active site binds both gases competitively, and their relative concentrations decide which binds. RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for CO₂ than for O₂ when the CO₂:O₂ ratio is nearly equal, so A is false.
steps: A: false, the affinity is greater for CO₂
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The membranes of the stroma lamellae contain both PS I and PS II.
Statement II: Cyclic photophosphorylation possibly takes place in the stroma lamellae, as they lack PS II and the enzyme NADP reductase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The membranes of the grana have both PS I and PS II, but the stroma lamellae lack PS II as well as NADP reductase. With only PS I working, the excited electron is cycled back, so the stroma lamellae are a likely site of cyclic photophosphorylation.
steps: Statement I: false, stroma lamellae lack PS II
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport (Cyclic and non-cyclic photo-phosphorylation)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following does NOT help to build up the proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane?

options.text: Splitting of water on the inner (lumen) side of the membrane
Flow of protons from the lumen to the stroma through the CF₀ channel of ATP synthase
Transfer of protons across the membrane as electrons move through the photosystems
Removal of protons from the stroma by NADP reductase during reduction of NADP⁺

solution.concept: Building and using the proton gradient
solution.explanation: Three events raise the proton concentration in the lumen relative to the stroma: water splitting on the lumen side, proton transport across the membrane by an H carrier as electrons pass, and removal of stroma protons by NADP reductase. The flow of protons back through CF₀ to the stroma breaks down the gradient; its energy is used by CF₁ to make ATP.
steps: Gradient built by: water splitting, H-carrier transport, NADP reductase
Gradient used by: proton flow through CF₀ → ATP
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are the NCERT list of events that create the gradient.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where are the ATP and NADPH used? / The Chemiosmotic Hypothesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: Flow of protons from the lumen to the stroma through the CF₀ channel of ATP synthase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which statement about the effect of temperature on photosynthesis is correct?

options.text: The light reactions are much more temperature sensitive than the dark reactions
C3 plants have a higher temperature optimum than C4 plants
The dark reactions, being enzymatic, are temperature controlled; the light reactions are affected to a much lesser extent
All plants have the same temperature optimum, whatever their habitat

solution.explanation: The dark reactions are enzymatic and so are temperature controlled; the light reactions are also temperature sensitive but much less so. C4 plants respond to higher temperatures and have a higher optimum than C3 plants, and the optimum depends on the habitat (tropical plants have a higher optimum than temperate ones).
steps: Enzymatic dark reactions → strongly temperature dependent
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options reverse the NCERT statements on light reactions, on C3 versus C4 plants, and on habitat.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Temperature)
solution.final_answer: Option C: The dark reactions, being enzymatic, are temperature controlled; the light reactions are affected to a much lesser extent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the electron transport in the light reaction are correct?

(a) Electrons excited in the reaction centre of PS II are picked up by an electron acceptor that passes them to an electron transport system consisting of cytochromes.
(b) The electrons move uphill, in terms of the redox potential scale, from PS II to PS I.
(c) The Z scheme gets its name from the shape formed when all the carriers are placed in sequence on a redox potential scale.
(d) The oxygen evolved in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide.
(e) The reaction centre is a single chlorophyll a molecule, and it is different in the two photosystems.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Electron transport and the Z scheme
solution.explanation: Excited electrons from PS II pass to an acceptor and then through cytochromes to PS I; this movement is downhill on the redox potential scale. Plotted on that scale, the carriers form a Z. Oxygen comes from the splitting of water, not CO₂. Each photosystem has a different chlorophyll a reaction centre (P680, P700).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (d) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport; Splitting of Water

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The productivity and yields of C4 plants are better than those of C3 plants.
Reason (R): C4 plants have a mechanism that increases the concentration of CO₂ at the site of RuBisCO, so photorespiration does not occur in them.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why C4 plants are more productive
solution.explanation: In C4 plants, decarboxylation of the C4 acid in bundle sheath cells raises the CO₂ concentration around RuBisCO, so the enzyme acts as a carboxylase and photorespiration does not occur. NCERT states that this explains why productivity and yields are better in these plants.
steps: Absence of photorespiration → better productivity → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: There is a linear relationship between incident light and the rate of CO₂ fixation at high light intensities.
Statement II: Water stress reduces photosynthesis because it causes the stomata to close, reducing CO₂ availability, and makes leaves wilt, reducing their surface area and metabolic activity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The relationship between incident light and CO₂ fixation is linear at low light intensities; at higher intensities the rate stops rising as other factors become limiting. Water affects photosynthesis mostly indirectly: water stress closes stomata (less CO₂) and makes leaves wilt.
steps: Statement I: false, linear only at low light
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Light; Water)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the C4 pathway, the C4 acid is broken down in the bundle sheath cells to release CO₂ and a 3-carbon molecule. In the mesophyll cells, this 3-carbon molecule is converted back to:

solution.explanation: In the bundle sheath, the C4 acid is decarboxylated; the CO₂ enters the Calvin cycle and the 3-carbon molecule returns to the mesophyll, where it is converted to PEP again, ready to accept CO₂.
steps: Bundle sheath: C4 acid → CO₂ + C3 molecule
solution.why_others_wrong: RuBP is regenerated in the Calvin cycle of the bundle sheath; OAA is the first product of fixation, not the regenerated acceptor; PGA is the product of RuBP carboxylation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant growing in deep shade on a dense forest floor is supplied with extra CO₂, but its rate of photosynthesis does not change. When the light falling on it is increased, the rate rises. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: CO₂ was the limiting factor, because CO₂ always limits photosynthesis
Light was the limiting factor, because the rate is set by the factor nearest to its minimal value
Light was the limiting factor, because light is limiting for all plants in nature
Neither factor was limiting; the rise was due to stomatal opening alone

solution.explanation: If a process is affected by more than one factor, its rate is determined by the factor nearest to its minimal value. Extra CO₂ had no effect, but more light raised the rate, so light was nearest its minimum. Light is rarely limiting in nature, except for plants in shade or in dense forests, which is the situation here.
steps: Raising CO₂: no change → CO₂ was not limiting
Raising light: rate rises → light was limiting
solution.why_others_wrong: Extra CO₂ had no effect, so CO₂ was not limiting here. Light is not limiting for all plants (light saturation occurs at about 10% of full sunlight); it limits here because the plant is in deep shade. The observed response to light shows a limiting factor was acting.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Law of limiting factors; Light)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Light was the limiting factor, because the rate is set by the factor nearest to its minimal value

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Glycolysis takes place in the:

solution.explanation: Glycolysis, the partial oxidation of glucose to two molecules of pyruvic acid, takes place in the cytoplasm and is present in all living organisms.
solution.why_others_wrong: The matrix is the site of the TCA cycle, the inner membrane of the ETS, and the stroma of the Calvin cycle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option C: cytoplasm of the cell

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In yeast, under anaerobic conditions, pyruvic acid is converted to:

solution.explanation: In fermentation, say by yeast, incomplete oxidation of glucose under anaerobic conditions converts pyruvic acid to CO₂ and ethanol. The enzymes pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase catalyse these reactions.
steps: Yeast, anaerobic: pyruvic acid → CO₂ + ethanol
solution.why_others_wrong: Lactic acid is formed by some bacteria and by muscle cells when oxygen is inadequate. Acetyl CoA is formed aerobically in mitochondria. Citric acid is a TCA cycle intermediate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Fermentation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA in the mitochondrial matrix is catalysed by:

solution.explanation: Pyruvate enters the mitochondrial matrix and undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by a complex set of reactions catalysed by pyruvic dehydrogenase, which needs several coenzymes including NAD⁺ and coenzyme A. Acetyl CoA, CO₂ and NADH are formed.
steps: Pyruvic acid + CoA + NAD⁺ → acetyl CoA + CO₂ + NADH + H⁺ (pyruvic dehydrogenase)
solution.why_others_wrong: Pyruvic acid decarboxylase acts in alcoholic fermentation; lactate dehydrogenase forms lactic acid; hexokinase phosphorylates glucose in glycolysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Aerobic Respiration

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Yeasts poison themselves to death when the concentration of alcohol reaches about 13 per cent.
Statement II: In plants, sucrose is converted into glucose and fructose by the enzyme hexokinase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Yeasts die when the alcohol they produce reaches about 13 per cent. In plants, glucose comes from sucrose (the end product of photosynthesis) or storage carbohydrates; sucrose is converted into glucose and fructose by invertase. Hexokinase phosphorylates glucose.
steps: Statement II: false, the enzyme is invertase
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis; Fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: During glycolysis of one molecule of glucose, ATP is used at two steps and is formed when BPGA is converted to PGA and when PEP is converted to pyruvic acid. How many ATP molecules are formed directly, and what is the net gain of ATP?

solution.explanation: One glucose splits into two triose phosphates, so each ATP-forming step occurs twice: BPGA → PGA gives 2 ATP and PEP → pyruvic acid gives 2 ATP, 4 in all. Two ATP are used (glucose → glucose-6-phosphate and fructose-6-phosphate → fructose 1,6-bisphosphate). Net gain = 4 − 2 = 2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 formed counts each step only once (forgetting the two trioses). Net gain 4 ignores the two ATP used. 2 formed with net 0 makes both mistakes together.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (compound) with List-II (number of carbon atoms).

List-I:
A. Pyruvic acid
B. Citric acid
C. α-Ketoglutaric acid
D. Malic acid

List-II:
I. Four
II. Five
III. Three
IV. Six

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Glycolysis gives the 3-carbon pyruvic acid. In the TCA cycle, the 2-carbon acetyl group joins the 4-carbon OAA to give 6-carbon citric acid; two decarboxylations give 5-carbon α-ketoglutaric acid and then the 4-carbon succinyl CoA; malic acid is a 4-carbon acid that is oxidised to OAA.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the 6- and 5-carbon acids, the 3- and 4-carbon acids, or α-ketoglutaric and malic acid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Tricarboxylic Acid Cycle (Figure: the Citric acid cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plants can get along without specialised respiratory organs.
Reason (R): Each plant part takes care of its own gas-exchange needs, and there is very little transport of gases from one plant part to another.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT gives this as the first reason plants manage without respiratory organs: each part meets its own gas-exchange needs with very little transport of gases between parts. (Plants also have low demands for gas exchange, and most living cells lie close to the surface.)
steps: R: true and is a stated reason → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Do Plants Breathe?
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the TCA cycle are correct?

(a) During the conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid, a molecule of GTP is synthesised.
(b) The TCA cycle takes place in the cytoplasm.
(c) There are three points in the cycle where NAD⁺ is reduced to NADH + H⁺ and one point where FAD⁺ is reduced to FADH₂.
(d) Two successive decarboxylations lead to the formation of α-ketoglutaric acid and then succinyl CoA.
(e) Citric acid is isomerised to malic acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The TCA cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix. Citrate is isomerised to isocitrate; two successive decarboxylations give α-ketoglutaric acid and then succinyl CoA. Succinyl CoA → succinic acid makes a GTP (substrate-level phosphorylation). NAD⁺ is reduced at three points and FAD⁺ at one.
steps: (e) false: citrate is isomerised to isocitrate
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Tricarboxylic Acid Cycle

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When fats are used as the respiratory substrate, the RQ is less than 1.
Statement II: When proteins are used as the respiratory substrate, the RQ is about 0.9.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: RQ depends on the substrate. For carbohydrates it is 1; for fats it is less than 1 (tripalmitin gives about 0.7); for proteins it is about 0.9.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Respiratory Quotient
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: One molecule of glucose is completely oxidised by aerobic respiration. How many molecules of CO₂ are released in all by the conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA and the TCA cycle together, and how many of these are released in the TCA cycle itself?

options.text: 6 in all; 6 in the TCA cycle
6 in all; 4 in the TCA cycle
3 in all; 2 in the TCA cycle
4 in all; 2 in the TCA cycle

solution.concept: Where the six CO₂ of glucose are released
solution.explanation: Glycolysis releases no CO₂ and gives 2 pyruvic acid. Each pyruvic acid loses one CO₂ when it becomes acetyl CoA (2 in all). Each acetyl CoA loses two CO₂ in the two decarboxylations of the TCA cycle (4 in all). Total 6, matching the 6 carbons of glucose.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 in the TCA cycle forgets the CO₂ of the link reaction. 3 and 2 counts one pyruvic acid instead of two. 4 and 2 counts the TCA cycle for only one acetyl CoA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Aerobic Respiration; Tricarboxylic Acid Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option B: 6 in all; 4 in the TCA cycle

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the respiratory balance sheet are correct?

(a) It assumes a sequential, orderly pathway, with one substrate forming the next and glycolysis, the TCA cycle and the ETS following one after another.
(b) It assumes that the NADH synthesised in glycolysis is oxidised in the cytoplasm without entering the mitochondria.
(c) It assumes that none of the intermediates in the pathway is used to synthesise any other compound.
(d) Its assumptions are fully valid in a living system.
(e) On these assumptions, there can be a net gain of 38 ATP molecules during aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The calculation assumes an orderly sequential pathway, that glycolytic NADH is transferred into the mitochondria for oxidative phosphorylation, that no intermediates are withdrawn, and that only glucose is respired. On these assumptions the net gain is 38 ATP per glucose. These assumptions are not really valid in a living system, where all pathways work simultaneously and substrates enter and leave as needed.
steps: (b) false: glycolytic NADH is assumed to enter the mitochondria
(d) false: the assumptions are not really valid in a living system
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (d) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', The Respiratory Balance Sheet

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Although the role of oxygen is limited to the terminal stage of aerobic respiration, its presence is vital.
Reason (R): Oxygen acts as the first hydrogen acceptor, receiving hydrogen during glycolysis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Oxygen acts only at the terminal stage, yet it is vital because it drives the whole process by removing hydrogen from the system; it is the final hydrogen acceptor. In glycolysis, hydrogen is accepted by NAD⁺, not oxygen, so R is false.
steps: R: false, oxygen is the final hydrogen acceptor; NAD⁺ accepts hydrogen in glycolysis
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In glycolysis, glucose undergoes partial oxidation to form two molecules of pyruvic acid.
Statement II: In both lactic acid and alcoholic fermentation, the reducing agent is NADH + H⁺, which is reoxidised to NAD⁺.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Glycolysis partially oxidises glucose to two pyruvic acid. In both lactic acid and alcohol fermentation, not much energy is released; the reducing agent NADH + H⁺ is reoxidised to NAD⁺, which keeps glycolysis going.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis; Fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: When a cell population grows geometrically in a limited nutrient supply and its growth is plotted against time, a sigmoid curve is obtained. In which phase of this curve is the growth fastest?

solution.explanation: In geometric growth the initial growth is slow (lag phase), then it increases rapidly at an exponential rate (log or exponential phase), when both progeny cells of each division keep dividing. With limited nutrients, growth then slows down and levels off in the stationary phase.
steps: Log/exponential phase: rapid growth, both daughter cells keep dividing
Stationary phase: growth slows because nutrients become limiting
solution.why_others_wrong: The lag and stationary phases are the slow parts of the curve. The phase of maturation is a zone of the growing root or shoot, not a phase of the sigmoid curve.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth rates: geometric growth and the sigmoid curve

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Grape growers use a plant growth regulator to increase the length of grape stalks. The regulator used is:

solution.explanation: Gibberellins cause an increase in the length of the axis. This ability is used commercially to increase the length of grape stalks.
steps: Increase in length of axis → gibberellins
solution.why_others_wrong: ABA is a growth inhibitor; ethylene promotes ripening and abscission; cytokinins promote cell division and lateral shoot growth, not axis elongation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', gibberellins: physiological effects

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Abscisic acid is also called the stress hormone because it increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses.
Statement II: Abscisic acid promotes seed germination.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: ABA acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. It inhibits seed germination, stimulates closure of stomata and increases tolerance to various stresses, which is why it is called the stress hormone.
steps: Statement II: false, ABA inhibits seed germination
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', abscisic acid
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Growth in plants can be measured as an increase in cell number. According to NCERT, a single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than:

solution.explanation: Growth at the cellular level is an increase in the amount of protoplasm, which is hard to measure directly, so other parameters are used. A single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour, whereas cells in a watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times.
steps: Maize root apical meristem → over 17,500 new cells per hour
3,50,000 is the increase in size of watermelon cells, not a cell count
solution.why_others_wrong: 3,50,000 refers to the increase in cell size in watermelon. The other options change the number or the time unit.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth is measurable
solution.final_answer: Option B: 17,500 new cells per hour

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) is widely applied in tea plantations and in hedge-making.
Reason (R): In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds; removing the shoot tip usually results in the growth of the lateral buds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Auxin produced by the growing apical bud suppresses the lateral buds (apical dominance). Decapitation removes this inhibition, so lateral buds grow and the plant becomes bushy. That is exactly why decapitation is used in tea plantations (more leafy shoots) and hedge-making (dense growth).
steps: A: true, NCERT's applications of decapitation
R: true, definition of apical dominance and effect of decapitation
Lateral buds grow after decapitation → bushy plants → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', auxins: apical dominance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Gibberellins cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve their shape.
Statement II: Cytokinins are used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both uses in the statements are uses of gibberellins: they elongate apple fruits and improve their shape, and they speed up malting in brewing. Cytokinins are not used for malting.
steps: Statement II: false, malting is speeded up by gibberellins, not cytokinins
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', gibberellins: physiological effects
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant growth regulator) with List-II (chemical nature).

List-I:
A. Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA)
B. Gibberellic acid (GA₃)
C. Abscisic acid (ABA)
D. Ethylene

List-II:
I. Gas
II. Terpene
III. Indole compound
IV. Derivative of carotenoids

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Chemical nature of plant growth regulators
solution.explanation: NCERT groups PGRs by chemical nature: indole compounds (IAA), adenine derivatives (kinetin), derivatives of carotenoids (ABA), terpenes (GA₃) and gases (ethylene, C₂H₄).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap terpene and carotenoid derivative between GA₃ and ABA, or call IAA a terpene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: characteristics
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about auxins are correct?

(a) Auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings.
(b) Auxins promote flowering, for example in pineapples.
(c) NAA and 2,4-D are natural auxins isolated from plants.
(d) Auxins control xylem differentiation and help in cell division.
(e) Auxins are produced mainly in mature leaves and roots and move to the growing apices.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Auxins are generally produced by the growing apices of stems and roots, from where they migrate to their regions of action. IAA and IBA are isolated from plants; NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins. Auxins initiate rooting in stem cuttings, promote flowering in pineapple, control xylem differentiation and help in cell division.
steps: (e) False: auxins are produced at the growing apices of stems and roots
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', auxins

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Differentiation in plants is closed, because cells derived from the same meristem always mature into the same kind of structure.
Statement II: Development in plants is under the control of intrinsic factors, such as genetic factors and plant growth regulators, as well as extrinsic factors such as light, temperature, water, oxygen and nutrition.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Open differentiation and control of development
solution.explanation: Differentiation in plants is open: cells or tissues arising from the same meristem have different structures at maturity. Development is controlled by intrinsic factors (intracellular genetic factors and intercellular chemicals such as PGRs) and by extrinsic factors (light, temperature, water, oxygen, nutrition).
steps: Statement I: false, differentiation in plants is open
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation; development
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A callus of mass 2 g grows geometrically according to W₁ = W₀e^(rt), with relative growth rate r = 0.231 per day. Taking ln 2 = 0.693, what will be its mass after 9 days?

solution.explanation: In geometric growth W₁ = W₀e^(rt). Here rt = 0.231 × 9 = 2.079 = 3 × 0.693 = 3 ln 2, so e^(rt) = 2³ = 8. W₁ = 2 g × 8 = 16 g.
solution.shortcut: rt is three times ln 2, so the callus doubles three times: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 g.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.2 g uses the arithmetic form W₀(1 + rt). 8 g is e^(rt) alone, forgetting to multiply by W₀. 12 g multiplies W₀ by 2 and by 3 instead of raising 2 to the power 3.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth rates: geometric growth

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about gibberellins are correct?

(a) More than 100 gibberellins have been reported from widely different organisms such as fungi and higher plants.
(b) All gibberellins are basic in nature.
(c) GA₃ was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form.
(d) Gibberellins delay senescence, so fruits can be left on the tree longer to extend the market period.
(e) Gibberellins are derivatives of carotenoids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: More than 100 gibberellins (GA₁, GA₂, GA₃ ...) are known from fungi and higher plants; GA₃ was one of the first discovered and is the most intensively studied. All GAs are acidic. They are terpenes; it is ABA that is a carotenoid derivative. Gibberellins delay senescence, which extends the market period of fruits.
steps: (e) False: GAs are terpenes; ABA is the carotenoid derivative
solution.why_others_wrong: Options B and D include (b); option C includes (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', gibberellins

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ethylene promotes vertical growth of seedlings and suppresses swelling of the axis.
Reason (R): Ethylene promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs, especially of leaves and flowers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Ethylene influences horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings, so the assertion reverses both effects. Ethylene does promote senescence and abscission of plant organs, especially leaves and flowers, so R is true.
steps: A: false, ethylene promotes horizontal growth and swelling of the axis
solution.why_others_wrong: A is the trap: it inverts the NCERT effects (horizontal growth, swelling of the axis).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', ethylene
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A grower wants a single compound that, applied as an aqueous spray, is readily absorbed and releases a growth regulator slowly inside the plant. It should hasten ripening of tomatoes and apples and accelerate abscission of flowers and fruits for thinning of cotton, cherry and walnut. The compound is:

solution.concept: Ethephon as a source of ethylene
solution.explanation: Ethephon is the most widely used compound as a source of ethylene. In aqueous solution it is readily absorbed and transported within the plant and releases ethylene slowly. Ethylene hastens fruit ripening (tomatoes, apples) and accelerates abscission of flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry, walnut).
steps: Effects described: ripening and abscission → ethylene
Compound that releases ethylene slowly in the plant → ethephon
solution.why_others_wrong: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin used as a herbicide. Gibberellic acid delays senescence of fruits. Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor and does not release ethylene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', ethylene

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed and each lobe is dithecous. How many microsporangia does such an anther have?

solution.explanation: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, each lobe having two theca (dithecous). The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure with four microsporangia at the corners, two in each lobe.
solution.why_others_wrong: Two counts only the lobes; one ignores both lobes and theca; eight doubles the real number.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The prominent apertures in the exine of a pollen grain, where sporopollenin is absent, are called:

solution.explanation: The exine of the pollen grain has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent. The pollen tube comes out through one of the germ pores when the pollen germinates.
steps: Exine with apertures lacking sporopollenin → germ pores
solution.why_others_wrong: The micropyle is the opening of the ovule, the hilum is the junction of ovule and funicle, and lenticels are openings in the bark of woody stems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Ovules generally differentiate a single megaspore mother cell (MMC). In which region of the nucellus is it differentiated?

solution.explanation: Ovules generally differentiate a single megaspore mother cell in the micropylar region of the nucellus. It is a large cell with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, and it undergoes meiosis to form four megaspores.
steps: MMC → large cell, dense cytoplasm, prominent nucleus
Location → micropylar region of the nucellus
solution.why_others_wrong: The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule opposite the micropyle; the hilum and funicle lie outside the nucellus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac: megasporogenesis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Among animals, the dominant biotic pollinating agents are:

solution.explanation: Bees, butterflies, flies, beetles, wasps, ants, moths, birds (sunbirds, hummingbirds) and bats are common pollinating agents, and some primates, arboreal rodents and reptiles also pollinate. Among the animals, insects, particularly bees, are the dominant biotic pollinating agents.
steps: Dominant biotic agents → insects, especially bees
solution.why_others_wrong: Birds, bats and rodents do pollinate some species, but none is the dominant group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the embryo sac, the fusion of one male gamete with the two polar nuclei is called:

solution.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the egg cell (syngamy) to form the diploid zygote. The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei in the central cell to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus; because three haploid nuclei are involved this is called triple fusion. The two fusions together make up double fertilisation.
steps: Male gamete + 2 polar nuclei → triple fusion
solution.why_others_wrong: Syngamy is fusion with the egg. Double fertilisation is the name for both fusions together. 'Generative fusion' is not a term NCERT uses.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as:

solution.explanation: Occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is called polyembryony. In many Citrus and mango varieties, nucellar cells develop into additional embryos.
steps: More than one embryo per seed → polyembryony
solution.why_others_wrong: Parthenocarpy is fruit formation without fertilisation; apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation; polyploidy is an increase in whole chromosome sets.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium is generally surrounded by four wall layers: the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum.
Statement II: Carrot grass (Parthenium), which came into India as a contaminant with imported wheat, has become ubiquitous and causes pollen allergy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A microsporangium appears near circular in section and is surrounded by four wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum. Pollen grains of many species cause severe allergies and bronchial afflictions; Parthenium, which entered India with imported wheat, is now ubiquitous and causes pollen allergy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of the ovule) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Funicle
B. Hilum
C. Micropyle
D. Chalaza

List-II:
I. Small opening at the tip where the integuments are absent
II. Stalk that attaches the ovule to the placenta
III. Basal part of the ovule, opposite the micropylar end
IV. Region where the body of the ovule fuses with the funicle

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The ovule is attached to the placenta by a stalk, the funicle. The body of the ovule fuses with the funicle at the hilum, the junction between ovule and funicle. The integuments encircle the nucellus except at the tip, where the micropyle is organised. Opposite the micropylar end is the chalaza, the basal part of the ovule.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap funicle with hilum, or micropyle with chalaza, the two pairs most often confused.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about insect-pollinated flowers are correct?

(a) The majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar.
(b) When the flowers are small, a number of them are clustered into an inflorescence to make them conspicuous.
(c) Their pollen grains are generally light, non-sticky and produced in enormous numbers.
(d) Their pollen grains are generally sticky.
(e) In some species, the floral reward is a safe place for the pollinator to lay its eggs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Insect-pollinated flowers are mostly large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar; small flowers are clustered into inflorescences to be conspicuous. Their pollen grains are generally sticky so they adhere to the pollinator's body. Rewards are nectar and pollen, and in some species a safe place to lay eggs (as in Amorphophallus and Yucca). Light, non-sticky pollen is a feature of wind-pollinated flowers.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The majority of flowering plants produce unisexual flowers, so pollen rarely comes in contact with the stigma of the same flower.
Statement II: Continued self-pollination results in inbreeding depression.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite (bisexual) flowers, so pollen grains are likely to contact the stigma of the same flower. Continued self-pollination results in inbreeding depression, which is why flowering plants have evolved devices that discourage self-pollination.
steps: Statement I: false, most flowering plants have hermaphrodite flowers
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', outbreeding devices
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In most flowering plants, endosperm development precedes embryo development.
Reason (R): The zygote divides immediately after fertilisation, before the primary endosperm cell starts dividing.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly to form the endosperm. Most zygotes divide only after a certain amount of endosperm is formed; this adaptation assures nutrition to the developing embryo. So A is true and R, which reverses the order, is false.
steps: R: false, most zygotes divide only after some endosperm has formed
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation events: endosperm and embryo
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, apomixis (production of seeds without fertilisation) is seen in:

options.text: Some species of Asteraceae and grasses
All dioecious plants such as papaya

solution.explanation: Some flowering plants, such as some species of Asteraceae and grasses, have evolved a special mechanism, apomixis, to produce seeds without fertilisation. It is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction.
steps: NCERT examples → some Asteraceae and grasses
solution.why_others_wrong: Pea and groundnut form seeds after fertilisation. Dioecy is an outbreeding device. Banana forms fruits without fertilisation (parthenocarpy), and these fruits are seedless.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony
solution.final_answer: Option B: Some species of Asteraceae and grasses

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A microsporangium contains 40 microspore mother cells, and all of them complete microsporogenesis normally. Each resulting pollen grain eventually forms the usual number of male gametes. How many male gametes are formed in all?

solution.explanation: Each microspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to form a tetrad of four microspores, each of which matures into a pollen grain. In each pollen grain the generative cell divides to form two male gametes.
solution.why_others_wrong: 160 counts pollen grains, not gametes. 80 assumes each mother cell gives two pollen grains. 640 assumes four gametes per pollen grain.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', microsporogenesis; pollen grain

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Scutellum
B. Coleoptile
C. Hypocotyl
D. Plumule

List-II:
I. Hollow foliar structure enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia in a grass embryo
II. Cylindrical part of the embryonal axis below the cotyledons, ending in the radicle
III. Stem tip at the end of the epicotyl
IV. Single cotyledon of the grass family, situated towards one side of the embryonal axis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In the grass family the single cotyledon is the scutellum, situated laterally on the embryonal axis. The epicotyl of a monocot embryo has the shoot apex and a few leaf primordia enclosed in a hollow foliar structure, the coleoptile. In a dicot embryo, the part of the axis below the cotyledons is the hypocotyl, ending in the radicle; the part above is the epicotyl, ending in the plumule (stem tip).
steps: Scutellum → single lateral cotyledon of grasses (A-IV)
Hypocotyl → below cotyledons, ends in radicle (C-II)
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap scutellum with coleoptile, or hypocotyl with plumule.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation events: embryo
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about events in the embryo sac during and after fertilisation are correct?

(a) The primary endosperm cell develops into the endosperm.
(b) The synergids and antipodals degenerate after fertilisation.
(c) The zygote develops into the embryo.
(d) The pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of an antipodal cell.
(e) The two male gametes are formed by division of the vegetative cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The pollen tube enters one of the synergids (guided by the filiform apparatus) and releases two male gametes into its cytoplasm. These male gametes were formed by division of the generative cell. After double fertilisation, the primary endosperm cell develops into the endosperm and the zygote into the embryo, while the synergids and antipodals degenerate.
steps: (d) False: the gametes are released into a synergid
(e) False: male gametes come from the generative cell
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, C and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation; post-fertilisation events

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Xenogamy is the only type of pollination that brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma.
Reason (R): In xenogamy, pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma of a different plant.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In autogamy pollen comes from the same flower, and in geitonogamy from another flower of the same plant; geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy because the pollen comes from the same plant. Only in xenogamy does pollen come from a different plant, so only xenogamy brings genetically different pollen to the stigma. R states that defining feature, so it explains A.
steps: R: true, pollen from a different plant
A different plant carries a different genotype → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: kinds of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In plants that shed pollen in the three-celled condition, the pollen tubes carry the two male gametes from the beginning.
Statement II: In plants that shed pollen in the two-celled condition, the generative cell divides to form the two male gametes before the pollen grain lands on the stigma.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: After a compatible pollen lands, it germinates and its tube grows through the stigma and style. Where pollen is shed at the three-celled stage, the tube carries the two male gametes from the beginning. Where it is shed at the two-celled stage, the generative cell divides to form the two male gametes during the growth of the pollen tube in the stigma, i.e. after the pollen has landed.
steps: Statement II: false, the division happens during pollen tube growth in the stigma
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II shifts the timing of the generative cell division; that detail is the trap.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollen-pistil interaction
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a flowering plant with 2n = 24, how many chromosomes are present in a cell of the nucellus, the functional megaspore, an endosperm cell and a synergid, respectively?

solution.concept: Ploidy of ovule and embryo sac tissues
solution.explanation: The nucellus is sporophytic tissue of the parent plant (2n = 24). The megaspore is formed by meiosis (n = 12). The synergid is part of the female gametophyte formed from the megaspore by mitosis (n = 12). The endosperm comes from the primary endosperm nucleus formed by triple fusion (3n = 36).
solution.why_others_wrong: A treats the nucellus as haploid and the synergid as diploid. B forgets that the megaspore forms by meiosis. C treats the endosperm as diploid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', megasporogenesis; double fertilisation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Parthenocarpy can be induced through the application of growth hormones, and such fruits are seedless.
(b) Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction.
(c) In some species, the diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and develops into the embryo without fertilisation.
(d) Parthenocarpic fruits contain seeds formed by apomixis.
(e) Apomixis is the development of a fruit without fertilisation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation; it can be induced by growth hormones and the fruits are seedless. Apomixis is the production of seeds without fertilisation, an asexual process mimicking sexual reproduction; in some species a diploid egg forms without reduction division and develops into the embryo without fertilisation.
steps: (e) False: that describes parthenocarpy; apomixis produces seeds
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony; parthenocarpy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In most water-pollinated species, the pollen grains are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering.
Reason (R): Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are NCERT facts about water pollination. The mucilaginous covering protects the pollen from getting wet in water. The rarity of water pollination (about 30 genera, mostly monocots) is a separate fact about its distribution and does not explain why the pollen has a protective covering.
steps: R is about how rare water pollination is, not about protecting pollen → B
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the trap: R is a true fact about the same topic but explains nothing about the mucilage.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Gregor Mendel conducted his hybridisation experiments on garden peas over a period of:

solution.explanation: Mendel conducted hybridisation experiments on garden peas for seven years (1856–1863) and proposed the laws of inheritance in living organisms.
steps: Duration of Mendel's pea experiments → seven years, 1856 to 1863
solution.why_others_wrong: The other periods do not match NCERT; 1900 is the year his work was rediscovered.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendel's laws of inheritance

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In 1900, Mendel's results on the inheritance of characters were independently rediscovered by:

options.text: de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak

solution.explanation: Mendel's work remained unrecognised for several decades. In 1900, three scientists, de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak, independently rediscovered his results on the inheritance of characters.
steps: 1900 → independent rediscovery by de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak
solution.why_others_wrong: Sutton and Boveri linked chromosome movement to Mendel's factors; Morgan and Sturtevant worked on linkage and gene mapping in Drosophila; Watson and Crick proposed the double helix of DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option A: de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Henking (1891) traced a specific nuclear structure all through spermatogenesis in a few insects and named it the 'X body'. What did he observe about its distribution?

options.text: All the sperm received the X body
All the eggs lacked the X body
The X body was found only in somatic cells
Only 50 per cent of the sperm received the X body after spermatogenesis

solution.explanation: Henking observed that 50 per cent of the sperm received this structure after spermatogenesis while the other 50 per cent did not. He named it the X body but could not explain its significance; later it was named the X chromosome.
steps: Structure traced through spermatogenesis → X body
Distribution → only half the sperm received it
solution.why_others_wrong: Henking studied spermatogenesis and found the structure in only half the sperm, not all; he made no observation about eggs or restriction to somatic cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination
solution.final_answer: Option D: Only 50 per cent of the sperm received the X body after spermatogenesis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: α-thalassemia is controlled by a single gene, HBB, on chromosome 11.
Statement II: Thalassemia is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules, whereas sickle-cell anaemia is a qualitative problem of synthesising an incorrectly functioning globin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Thalassemia is an autosome-linked recessive blood disease. α-thalassemia is controlled by two closely linked genes, HBA1 and HBA2, on chromosome 16; β-thalassemia is controlled by a single gene, HBB, on chromosome 11. Thalassemia is a quantitative problem (too few globin molecules) while sickle-cell anaemia is a qualitative problem (incorrectly functioning globin).
steps: Statement I: false, it describes β-thalassemia; α-thalassemia: HBA1 and HBA2 on chromosome 16
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendelian disorders: thalassemia
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Failure of segregation of chromatids during the cell division cycle, resulting in the gain or loss of a chromosome, is called:

solution.explanation: Chromosomal disorders are caused by absence, excess or abnormal arrangement of chromosomes. Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division results in gain or loss of one or more chromosomes, called aneuploidy (as in Down's syndrome).
steps: Gain or loss of individual chromosome(s) → aneuploidy
solution.why_others_wrong: Polyploidy is an increase in a whole set of chromosomes; a point mutation changes a single base; crossing over exchanges segments between homologous chromosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal disorders

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Multiple alleles can be found only when population studies are made.
Statement II: A single diploid individual can carry more than two alleles of the same gene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
